title: Reduced dominant part over an integral base
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $S$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Form the union of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] $Z$ of $X$ whose image is dense in $S$ (dominance as in [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]), and take its closure. The reduced dominant part of $X$ over $S$ is this closed subset with its reduced induced scheme structure [def-pc-reduced-scheme], defined by its vanishing ideal sheaf, with the canonical closed immersion into $X$. When $X$ is Noetherian and $S$ integral this is the reduced union of the components dominating $S$, denoted $X_{\mathrm{md}}$ in ILO II 1.2.5.

source.place: Expose II 1.2.5--1.2.8, printed pp. 25--26; for integral S the maximally dominant components are precisely the components with dense image.
